text: This is Nova Wheels. Not a rental counter... not a spreadsheet. A complete system, built to make your fleet look like this. And run like this.

Your customers land here first. Every car, every rate, every rule, presented the way a Porsche or Lamborghini showroom would present it. It opens with a cinematic reveal, the menu moves like a luxury app, and every page glides. Because the first impression... sets the price.
Each vehicle gets its own page. Specs. Daily, weekly and monthly rates. Included miles, the deposit, all of it up front. So renters stop asking questions, and start booking.
Booking takes four screens. Which car. Which dates, with a live estimate. How to reach them. Done. The request lands in your dashboard, with a name and a number attached.

Now, the part your customers never see. Your operation. Sign in, and the first time through, it sets itself up like a new phone. Your company. Your lot. Your house rules. How you take money. Eight questions, and you're live.
Every morning starts here. What's out. What's due back. Who owes you. What still needs a signature. One screen. No digging.
And this is the heart of it. Handle a rental. One question per screen. Which car? Pick it from the fleet. Or if it's brand new, type the VIN, and it decodes itself.

Odometer, fuel, every pre-existing mark, photographed and timestamped before the keys move. Then the renter. Name. Contact. License, with an age gate for every car. An address that autocompletes. Insurance you verify on the spot. If they've rented before, one tap pulls their file. And if they're flagged do-not-rent... the system stops you cold.

Then, the money. Term, rate, mileage, deposit, down payment, and how they pay. Card on file is the default, because it's the only method that lets you recover tolls, tickets and damage after the car is back. Pick Zelle or cash, and it warns you, and still requires a card for incidentals. That is the difference between a business... and a hobby.

Every answer flows straight into the contract. Eighteen clauses written to protect the owner. Late returns. Prohibited use. GPS consent. Loss of use. Chargeback language. And under each one, a plain-English line, so the renter can never say they didn't understand.
Sign right there on the screen, or send a link. On their phone, they initial each money clause, read the rules, and sign. You get a timestamp, their device, and a countersign button.

When the car comes back, check-in does the math. Miles over. Fuel short. Hours late. Cleaning, smoking. All computed and itemized against the deposit. GPS and starter interrupt live right on the rental, with a log of every action. And payments... every installment, every deduction, across every rental, in one ledger. So when it's time to talk to a bank, or apply for funding, your numbers are already organized.

So what does this actually do for the business? It lets customers book from the website, instead of your DMs. It makes you look like a brand people expect to pay more for. It puts every dollar in writing before the keys move. And it turns a stack of paperwork into six minutes on a screen. Nova Wheels. Let's put it to work.
